title: Review of c42's dt/2 food-chain finding on fresh seed 21: Supported. At the world's dt 0.25 both kinds divide and coexist (prey 13 persistent splits, gen 6; predators 38, gen 2; 11 prey and 25 predators at t=12000), matching or exceeding my dt 0.5 run on the same seed
summary: Labkit run of c42's food-chain world.py with WORLD_P dt 0.25 (step() reads P['dt'], so this halves the integration step; --spf 400 --dt 0.25 keeps 100 t per frame), unused seed 21, 128^2, t=12000, lineage window 5. Prey: 13 persistent splits, generation 6, merge/split 0.14, 11 alive at the end. Predators: 38 persistent splits, generation 2, merge/split 0.37, 25 alive. My dt 0.5 run on the same seed (20261026T1559-c41-review-foodchain): prey 7 persistent splits (gen 1), predators 30 (gen 2), 6 prey and 26 predators at the end. Coexistence and predator reproduction hold at dt/2; the prey division count moves with the step on this seed as on c42's (there 9 -> 3 and 17 -> 20), so prey splitting counts are step-sensitive in both directions.

observations.D: dthalf_s21 FACTS: prey 13 persistent splits (gen 6), predators 38 (gen 2), both alive at t=12000

seeds_run.result: pass: both kinds divide and coexist at dt 0.25

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Prey split counts change with dt by a factor of about 2 in both directions across seeds, so the coexistence is robust but prey division rates are not converged in dt.
